_meta.note: Curated mechanism-of-action graphs for common drugs. Graph content is standard pharmacology cross-checked against FDA label Clinical Pharmacology / Mechanism of Action sections. Educational use only.

ibuprofen.summary: Ibuprofen inhibits cyclooxygenase-1 and -2 (COX-1/COX-2), reducing conversion of arachidonic acid to prostaglandin precursors. Lower prostaglandin levels diminish pain, fever and inflammation signaling.

citations.label: FDA label — Ibuprofen, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY (COX inhibition)

nodes.label: Ibuprofen
nodes.note: Non-selective NSAID; inhibits both COX isoforms reversibly.

nodes.label: Arachidonic acid
nodes.note: Membrane phospholipid released by phospholipase A2 at injury/inflammation sites.

nodes.label: COX-1
nodes.note: Constitutive enzyme producing prostaglandins that protect gastric mucosa and support platelet aggregation (TXA2).

nodes.label: COX-2
nodes.note: Inducible enzyme at inflammation sites; produces prostaglandins mediating pain, fever and inflammation.

nodes.label: Prostaglandins (PGE2 etc.)
nodes.note: Lipid mediators that sensitize pain receptors, act on the hypothalamic heat set-point, and sustain inflammation.

nodes.label: Pain & fever
nodes.note: Analgesic/antipyretic target — reduced when PGE2 synthesis falls.

nodes.label: Inflammation
nodes.note: Anti-inflammatory target of COX-2 inhibition.

nodes.label: Gastric mucosal protection
nodes.note: COX-1 prostaglandins maintain mucus/bicarbonate barrier — inhibition explains GI risk.

warfarin.summary: Warfarin inhibits VKORC1, blocking regeneration of reduced vitamin K needed to gamma-carboxylate clotting factors II, VII, IX and X. Without carboxylation these factors cannot bind phospholipid surfaces, so coagulation is impaired.

citations.label: FDA label — Warfarin, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY (vitamin K epoxide reductase)

nodes.label: Warfarin
nodes.note: Coumarin anticoagulant; S-warfarin metabolized by CYP2C9 — many interactions.

nodes.label: VKORC1
nodes.note: Vitamin K epoxide reductase — recycles oxidized vitamin K back to its reduced form.

nodes.label: Reduced vitamin K
nodes.note: Cofactor for gamma-glutamyl carboxylase.

nodes.label: Factors II, VII, IX, X
nodes.note: Vitamin K-dependent clotting factors; require gamma-carboxylation to function.

nodes.label: Effective coagulation
nodes.note: Impaired as functional factor levels fall (delayed onset ~days).

nodes.label: Reduced thromboembolism
nodes.note: Therapeutic goal in AF, VTE, mechanical valves.

nodes.label: Bleeding risk
nodes.note: Major adverse effect; potentiated by NSAIDs, antibiotics, amiodarone, etc.

metformin.summary: Metformin inhibits mitochondrial complex I, raising the AMP/ATP ratio and activating AMPK. The result is suppressed hepatic gluconeogenesis and increased peripheral insulin sensitivity, lowering blood glucose without causing hypoglycemia.

citations.label: FDA label — Metformin, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY (AMPK, hepatic glucose)

nodes.label: Metformin
nodes.note: First-line type 2 diabetes agent; renally excreted unchanged.

nodes.label: Mitochondrial complex I
nodes.note: Inhibition lowers ATP, raises AMP in hepatocytes.

nodes.label: AMPK
nodes.note: Cellular energy sensor activated by high AMP/ATP ratio.

nodes.label: Hepatic gluconeogenesis
nodes.note: Major driver of fasting hyperglycemia in T2DM.

nodes.label: Peripheral insulin sensitivity
nodes.note: Secondary effect increasing muscle glucose uptake.

nodes.label: Lower blood glucose
nodes.note: Net therapeutic effect; no hypoglycemia alone.

nodes.label: Lactic acidosis (rare)
nodes.note: Risk in renal impairment/hypoxia — boxed warning; metformin accumulates when eGFR <30.

atorvastatin.summary: Atorvastatin competitively inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting step of hepatic cholesterol synthesis. Liver cells respond by upregulating LDL receptors, clearing more LDL from plasma and lowering cardiovascular risk.

nodes.label: Atorvastatin
nodes.note: Potent, long-acting statin; CYP3A4 substrate.

nodes.label: HMG-CoA reductase
nodes.note: Rate-limiting enzyme of the mevalonate cholesterol pathway.

nodes.label: Mevalonate
nodes.note: Product of HMG-CoA reduction; precursor of cholesterol.

nodes.label: Hepatic cholesterol pool
nodes.note: Falls when synthesis is blocked.

nodes.label: LDL receptor (hepatocyte)
nodes.note: SREBP-2 upregulates surface LDL receptors when intracellular sterol drops.

nodes.label: Plasma LDL-C
nodes.note: Cleared faster via receptor-mediated uptake.

nodes.label: Atherosclerotic CV events
nodes.note: Reduced with sustained LDL lowering.

nodes.label: Myopathy / rhabdomyolysis
nodes.note: Class adverse effect; risk ↑ with CYP3A4 inhibitors, fibrates.

simvastatin.summary: Simvastatin (a lactone prodrug hydrolyzed to its active beta-hydroxy acid) inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, reducing hepatic cholesterol synthesis and upregulating LDL receptors. It is a major CYP3A4 substrate — strong inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin) sharply raise exposure and myopathy risk.

citations.label: FDA label — Simvastatin, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY & DRUG INTERACTIONS (CYP3A4)

nodes.label: Simvastatin (prodrug)
nodes.note: Lactone hydrolyzed to active acid; high CYP3A4 dependence.

nodes.label: CYP3A4
nodes.note: Clears active metabolite; inhibited by macrolides, azoles, protease inhibitors, grapefruit.

nodes.label: HMG-CoA reductase
nodes.note: Target enzyme of the statin class.

nodes.label: Hepatic cholesterol synthesis
nodes.note: Rate-limited by HMG-CoA reductase.

nodes.label: LDL receptor upregulation
nodes.note: Compensatory response to low intracellular sterol.

nodes.label: Plasma LDL-C ↓
nodes.note: Therapeutic effect.

nodes.label: Myopathy → rhabdomyolysis
nodes.note: Exposure-dependent; ↑CK, myoglobinuria, AKI risk.

lisinopril.summary: Lisinopril inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme, blocking conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II. Less angiotensin II means vasodilation and reduced aldosterone; ACE inhibition also raises bradykinin, contributing to cough and, rarely, angioedema.

nodes.label: Lisinopril
nodes.note: Long-acting ACE inhibitor; not metabolized, renally excreted.

nodes.label: ACE (kininase II)
nodes.note: Converts angiotensin I → II and degrades bradykinin.

nodes.label: Angiotensin I
nodes.note: Formed from angiotensinogen by renin.

nodes.label: Angiotensin II
nodes.note: Potent vasoconstrictor; stimulates aldosterone release.

nodes.label: Aldosterone
nodes.note: Sodium/water retention and K+ excretion; falls with ACE inhibition (hyperkalemia risk).

nodes.label: Bradykinin ↑
nodes.note: Accumulates when ACE is blocked; mediates cough/angioedema.

nodes.label: Blood pressure ↓
nodes.note: Therapeutic effect via vasodilation + natriuresis.

omeprazole.summary: Omeprazole is a weak-base prodrug activated in the acidic canaliculi of parietal cells, where it forms an irreversible disulfide bond with the H+/K+-ATPase. Pump inhibition suppresses basal and stimulated gastric acid secretion for ~24-48 h.

nodes.label: Omeprazole (prodrug)
nodes.note: Accumulates in acidic parietal canaliculi; CYP2C19 activation matters.

nodes.label: H+/K+-ATPase
nodes.note: Final common step of acid secretion; irreversibly inhibited.

nodes.label: Gastric acid secretion
nodes.note: Both basal and meal-stimulated secretion drop.

nodes.label: Luminal pH ↑
nodes.note: Less acid → higher intragastric pH.

nodes.label: Ulcer healing / GERD relief
nodes.note: Therapeutic effect.

nodes.label: ↑ C. difficile / fracture risk (long-term)
nodes.note: Consequence of prolonged acid suppression.

amoxicillin.summary: Amoxicillin binds penicillin-binding proteins (transpeptidases), blocking peptidoglycan cross-linking in the bacterial cell wall. Weakened walls and unchecked autolysins lead to osmotic lysis of dividing bacteria.

nodes.label: Amoxicillin
nodes.note: Beta-lactam; stable to gastric acid, good oral bioavailability.

nodes.label: PBPs (transpeptidases)
nodes.note: Membrane enzymes cross-linking peptidoglycan.

nodes.label: Peptidoglycan cross-linking
nodes.note: Blocked → structurally weak wall.

nodes.label: Bacterial cell wall integrity
nodes.note: Loss exposes osmotic fragility.

nodes.label: Bacterial lysis (bactericidal)
nodes.note: Net killing of susceptible organisms.

nodes.label: Beta-lactamase resistance
nodes.note: Common escape route — why clavulanate combos exist.

salbutamol.summary: Salbutamol stimulates airway beta-2 adrenergic receptors, raising cAMP via adenylyl cyclase. cAMP-dependent PKA signaling relaxes airway smooth muscle (bronchodilation); spillover onto skeletal-muscle and cardiac beta receptors causes tremor and tachycardia.

citations.label: FDA label — Albuterol sulfate, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY

nodes.label: Salbutamol / Albuterol
nodes.note: Inhaled SABA; selective for beta-2 at therapeutic doses.

nodes.label: β2-adrenergic receptor
nodes.note: Gs-coupled GPCR on airway smooth muscle.

nodes.label: Adenylyl cyclase (Gs)
nodes.note: Activates upon receptor stimulation.

nodes.label: cAMP ↑ / PKA
nodes.note: Second messenger; PKA lowers intracellular Ca2+ and desensitizes MLCK.

nodes.label: Smooth-muscle relaxation
nodes.note: Airway caliber increases.

nodes.label: Bronchodilation (relief)
nodes.note: Rapid rescue effect in asthma/COPD.

nodes.label: Tremor / tachycardia
nodes.note: Dose-limiting beta effects in skeletal muscle and heart.

aspirin.summary: Aspirin acetylates COX-1 in platelets, irreversibly blocking thromboxane A2 production for the platelet's lifespan (7-10 days) — the basis of its antiplatelet cardioprotection. Higher doses add COX-2 inhibition for analgesia; gastric prostaglandin loss drives GI bleeding risk.

nodes.label: Aspirin
nodes.note: Acetylates a serine residue in the COX channel.

nodes.label: COX-1 (platelet)
nodes.note: Anucleate platelets cannot resynthesize it — inhibition lasts the cell's life.

nodes.label: Thromboxane A2
nodes.note: Potent platelet activator and vasoconstrictor.

nodes.label: Platelet aggregation
nodes.note: Dampened → antiplatelet effect.

nodes.label: ↓ MI / stroke events
nodes.note: Goal of low-dose therapy.

nodes.label: COX-2 (higher doses)
nodes.note: Adds anti-inflammatory/analgesic effect at analgesic doses.

nodes.label: GI erosion / bleeding
nodes.note: Loss of mucosal prostaglandins + antiplatelet effect.
